name: Mare aux Vacoas
notes: Largest reservoir in Mauritius, south of Curepipe. Supplies the upper Plaines Wilhems and Moka. Dam raised several times (1892, 1915, 1928, 1961); gross storage of 25.89 Mm³ set by the 1996 hydrographic survey. Fed by the Tatamaka, Parc aux Cerfs and Pradier canals and the Arnaud diversion.

name: Midlands Dam
notes: Built on Grand River South East near Midlands village as buffer storage for La Nicolière; water is released down the 27 km La Nicolière Feeder Canal to supply the north of the island.

name: Bagatelle Dam
notes: Built 2012–2017, fed mainly by River Terre Rouge and River Cascade. Supplies Port Louis and the lower Plaines Wilhems (Quatre Bornes, Rose Hill, Stanley, Beau Bassin, Coromandel).

name: La Ferme
notes: At Bambous, built 1914–1918. Fed by the Trianon–Grosses Roches and La Fenêtre feeder canals. Used for irrigation, so its level is usually the lowest of the seven.

name: Mare Longue
notes: Fed mainly by River des Aigrettes. Since October 2011 its water is diverted to the La Marie treatment plant for domestic supply.

name: La Nicolière
notes: Built across Rivière du Rempart near Grande Rosalie. Main source for the northern districts and part of Port Louis; topped up from Midlands Dam through the La Nicolière Feeder Canal.

name: Piton du Milieu
notes: Smallest of the seven. Fed by River Vacoas and River Bateau; supplies the east of the island.
